papers.title_en: Personalized Scorer Modeling: A Learning-Based Framework for Deriving Robust Sleep Stage Labels from Multiple Experts
papers.authors: Seyyed Ali Hoseini, Javad Baseri, Hamid Saadatfar, Edris Hoseini Gol, AmirHossein Eshghi
papers.evidence: 睡眠分期、EEG、评分员间差异
papers.tldr: 自动睡眠分期通常以单一参考hypnogram为金标准，但专家间评分差异影响可靠性。本文提出学习型hypnogram（LBH），通过混淆矩阵建模每位评分者的阶段特定行为，并聚合多专家概率生成最终标签。在DOD-H和DOD-O上，随机森林结合EEG+EMG达到约86%准确率、85%F1，优于数据集hypnogram与最佳评分者。结果表明个性化评分者建模能构建更稳健的参考标签，保留全部专家信息。
papers.abstract_en: Sleep stage classification is important for the diagnosis and management of sleep disorders, yet most automatic staging studies evaluate models against a single reference hypnogram despite known inter-scorer variability. This study investigates whether multi-scored datasets can be used to construct more reliable reference labels from the collective behavior of multiple experts. We use the publicly available DOD-H and DOD-O datasets. EEG (C3-M2) and chin EMG signals were segmented into 30-s epochs, and 30 features were extracted from each modality, yielding 60 features for EEG+EMG. We propose a learning-based hypnogram (LBH) that models the stage-specific behavior of each scorer using confusion matrices derived from machine-learning models. After column normalization, these matrices estimate the probability of each true sleep stage given each scorer's label; probabilities are aggregated across scorers to assign the final label for each epoch. LBH was evaluated with random forest, support vector machine, and multilayer perceptron classifiers under EEG-only and EEG+EMG settings, and compared with the dataset hypnogram (DH) and best-scorer hypnogram (BSH). LBH consistently improved overall performance. The best results were obtained with random forest and EEG+EMG, reaching 86.07% accuracy, 85.46% precision, and 85.29% F1-score on DOD-H, and 86.04% accuracy, 85.21% precision, and 84.70% F1-score on DOD-O. These findings suggest that personalized scorer modeling can improve reference hypnogram construction without discarding information from individual experts.

papers.title_en: Decoding Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell RNA Velocity
papers.evidence: 提供了一种从单细胞RNA速率重建基因调控网络的数学框架，可迁移用于研究冬眠的分子机制
papers.tldr: 单细胞RNA速度记录了细胞状态的动态方向，但能否从中恢复隐藏的基因调控网络仍是开放问题。本文将该问题形式化为转录-剪接耦合的稀疏动态逆问题，从数学上证明：仅凭被动快照观测，调控作用不可唯一识别。进一步，本文提出受控扰动策略可恢复可识别性，并设计积分重建算法以避免数值微分，同时给出有限样本下的稀疏恢复保证。这一框架为理解单细胞数据解码调控网络的边界、指导扰动实验设计及预测细胞响应奠定了理论基础。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell RNA sequencing provides snapshots of cellular states, while RNA velocity offers directional information about their temporal evolution. A fundamental question is whether hidden gene regulatory networks governing cellular dynamics can be recovered from such incomplete observations. In this work, we develop a mathematical framework for regulatory network reconstruction from RNA velocity data by formulating the problem as a sparse dynamical inverse problem arising from coupled transcription-splicing dynamics. We show that passive snapshot observations are generally insufficient to uniquely identify regulatory interactions, revealing an intrinsic limitation of unperturbed measurements. We then prove that controlled perturbations restore identifiability by generating informative regulatory trajectories and characterize conditions for unique recovery. To address noisy and imperfect observations, we introduce an integral reconstruction approach that avoids numerical differentiation and establish finite-sample guarantees for sparse network recovery. Our results provide a mathematical foundation for understanding when and how gene regulatory networks can be decoded from single-cell observations, linking perturbation design, inverse problem theory, and predictive modeling of cellular responses.
